papers.title: SBi3PCF: cosmology with Dark Energy Survey Year 3 cosmic shear
papers.abstract: We present the first cosmic shear data analysis of the integrated 3-point correlation function (i3PCF), a higher-order weak lensing statistic, and the first simulation-based inference (SBI) analysis of a three-point cosmic shear correlation function on survey data. Using SBi3PCF, our previously developed SBI framework for the i3PCF, we jointly constrain the $w$CDM parameter space with the cosmic shear 2-point correlation functions $\xi_\pm$ (2PCFs) and the i3PCFs $\zeta_\pm$ from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3) weak lensing shape catalogue, from which we detect $\zeta_\pm$ with a signal-to-noise ratio of 12.8. Our forward model is built on the CosmoGridV1 N-body simulations and includes the survey mask, shape noise, intrinsic alignment, baryonic feedback, photometric redshift uncertainty and shear calibration bias. The analysis was carried out blind, with all choices frozen, and only unblinded once coverage tests, tests of the accuracy of the learned likelihoods, and internal consistency tests had been passed. For the joint $\xi_\pm$ + $\zeta_\pm$ analysis we obtain $\Omega_m = 0.272^{+0.038}_{-0.033}$, $S_8 = 0.784^{+0.024}_{-0.021}$ and $w_0 = -1.04^{+0.25}_{-0.19}$. Adding $\zeta_\pm$ improves the figure of merit in the $\Omega_m$-$S_8$-$w_0$ parameter space by a factor of $1.59$ over $\xi_\pm$ alone, as predicted by simulated i3PCF analyses. This gain comes from third-order information on angular scales $\geq 15'$ and aperture radii $\geq 50'$, a regime where baryonic effects are subdominant. The constraints are consistent with the other DES Y3 analyses of the same catalogue and with independent lensing analyses, and differ by at most $2.4\sigma$ from CMB and BAO data (Planck 2018 + BAO, in $\Omega_m$-$S_8$-$w_0$). This shows that $\zeta_\pm$ can be analysed on cosmological survey data with a fully simulation-based approach, an important step towards Stage-IV surveys.

papers.title: Deconfinement Confined to the Heaviest Neutron Stars: Strange Quark Matter from a Flavor-Dressed Contact Interaction
papers.abstract: We study cold, electrically neutral, beta-equilibrated quark matter with u, d, and s quarks described by a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose parameters are fixed in vacuum. The vector repulsion is varied as a fraction 0 < eta < 3/2 of the scalar coupling, and results are given with and without the flavor dressing of the effective coupling. Pure quark matter is not self-bound in this model, and no value of eta produces a star that reaches two solar masses while satisfying the tidal constraint from GW170817; the heaviest configurations owe their mass to an envelope of constituent quarks. We then construct hybrid stars with a relativistic mean-field hadronic phase fitted to GM1 saturation properties, using both Maxwell and Gibbs constructions and a deconfinement bag shift. Tying deconfinement to chiral restoration and requiring a continuous pressure yields an upper bound on this shift. Within that bound, quark matter appears inside stable stars only for eta < 1/2, never below about 4 n0, and only in stars between 2.2 and 2.35Msun, over a stable mass window of at most 0.02Msun. The vector strength that pure quark stars need to become massive prevents deconfinement in hybrid stars. Radii and tidal deformabilities of intermediate-mass stars are therefore set by the hadronic EoS alone; with the softer SLy4 EoS the transition moves to the maximum-mass configuration itself.

papers.title: Beyond just a torus? Re-contextualising the AGN type paradigm using data-driven host galaxy quenching histories
papers.abstract: The orientation of a dusty torus within a unified model explains the presence (Type-1) or absence (Type-2) of broad emission lines in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) spectra. This orientation-based unified model, however, fails to explain differences in host galaxy properties, such as star formation rates, of Type-1 and Type-2 AGNs. Star-formation histories (SFHs) can shed light on the connection between AGN type and host galaxy properties, but are challenging to extract from Type-1 AGN that outshine their host galaxies. We use mean-field independent component analysis (MFICA) spectrum decomposition to extract the stellar populations of $\sim$3000 optically selected Type-1 and Type-2 AGN host galaxies from the seventh data release (DR7) of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), matched in redshift ($0.16 \leq z \leq 0.4$) and AGN luminosity ($6.5<\log_{10} [L_{[OIII]}/L_\odot] <9.5$). Using MFICA, we find that only $\sim$10 per cent of AGN host galaxies have recently ($\lesssim1$\,Gyr) and rapidly quenched star formation following a starburst, with Type-2 AGN host galaxies having done so at most 100\,Myrs more recently than Type-1 AGN host galaxies. For most ($\sim$90 per cent) AGN hosts with normal recent star formation histories, Type-2 AGNs are associated with slightly younger stellar populations than Type-1 AGNs. The younger stellar populations of Type-2 AGN hosts can be explained by a link between dusty torus covering factors and stellar populations, by host-galaxy obscuration of AGN, or by an evolution in AGN type without major bursts or rapid quenching of star formation.

papers.title: Mapping large-scale structure without galaxy formation - combining fast radio bursts with CMB lensing
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are an emerging precision probe of cosmological fluctuations. The amount and quality of observed FRB data will grow enormously over the next decade. FRB dispersion data directly probe the free electron distribution up to intergalactic scales. Precision models of the free electron distribution are necessary to exploit this exciting new probe of large-scale structure. We show that the free electron distribution almost exactly follows the total matter distribution. We confirm this fact by estimating the electron field-level bias parameters for the first time from the FLAMINGO simulations. With simulation-based knowledge of a handful of electron free parameters, the electron distribution largely acts as a second realization of the matter distribution. Working on large scales, we can leverage this fact to combine FRB correlations with those of Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) weak lensing to constrain cosmological parameters. Assuming access to localized FRBs with redshifts, we perform cosmological forecasts using these two large-scale matter probes, which have no strong dependence on baryonic feedback models nor on parameters that encode galaxy formation. We show that the parameters $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_m$ are constrained at a level similar to or better than that obtained by combining FRB dispersion with weak lensing of galaxy shapes under conservative assumptions. These results motivate the use of FRB data as a complementary probe of cosmic structure and will be especially compelling as redshifts become available for localized FRB host galaxies.

papers.title: UV spectra of little red dots: Broad-line N/C, gas recycling and black hole masses
papers.abstract: Radiative-transfer models of supermassive black holes accreting inside dense gas cocoons reproduce the X-ray-to-near-infrared spectral energy distribution of "little red dots" (LRDs) using the code Sirocco. In the ultraviolet, these models also predict weak broad emission lines and a series of metal absorption lines, which deep spectroscopy from the JWST SPURS survey now detects in several LRDs. Here we use the models to interpret these features. We find that N and C ions of equal charge (3+ or 2+) occupy largely the same gas in the simulations, such that the combination of the broad N IV]/C IV and N III]/C III] flux ratios simultaneously constrains both the electron density and the N/C abundance ratio of the gas in the LRD proper. The nitrogen and carbon emission of SPURS-GN-2, an LRD at $z=7.19$, requires an order of magnitude nitrogen excess compared to the solar value, N/C $= 12^{+3}_{-2}$ (N/C)$_\odot$, in the broad-line gas with electron density $\log n_e = 9.7^{+0.3}_{-0.5}$ cm$^{-3}$. Thus, around half the broad-line CNO nuclei have passed through hydrogen burning. Because the ionised gas is replaced on a century timescale, sustaining this enrichment favours gas recycling. UV absorption lines test this independently. In two of the four LRDs, line blueshift velocities clearly increase with the photon energy required to ionise the absorber gas. In the models the absorption lines are spatially stratified, indicating that the gas is launched near the escape speed and slowed by gravity. In GN-2, where the measurement can be made, the inferred deceleration requires radiation pressure close to the Eddington limit of a $10^{6-7}$ M$_\odot$ black hole. The lines are also typically strongly saturated, making inferences of direct abundance ratios misleading.

papers.title: Bright Siren Cosmology Beyond Fisher: DALI Forecasts for Third-Generation Gravitational Wave Observatories
papers.abstract: In this work we assess non-Gaussian extensions of Fisher forecasting based on the Derivative Approximation for Likelihoods (DALI). We simulate ensembles of bright siren catalogs for third-generation observatories, adopting a Cosmic Explorer (CE) and a triangular Einstein Telescope (ET) network, frequency-domain inspiral waveforms, and selection-motivated priors for counterpart detection. We reconstruct approximate likelihoods using Fisher and the first DALI correction (Doublet), and propagate the inferred distance information to cosmological inference in a w0waCDM model. We find that the Doublet approximation provides tighter cosmological constraints than the Fisher approximation, reducing the inferred uncertainties by approximately a factor of two in agreement with non-approximate likelihood (called Exact) results. For our GW network onfiguration, 300 bright-siren detections up to z=1 yield an H0 precision of ~2.7% with the Doublet approximation, compared with ~2.5% for the exact likelihood. The adopted non-Gaussian GW priors induce a systematic displacement of the inferred luminosity distances from the fiducial values, which is also present in the exact GW reconstruction and propagates into the cosmological parameters. Compared with the exact cosmological likelihood, the Doublet results differ by only ~10% on average in the parameter uncertainties, compared with ~195% for the traditional Fisher approximation. The Doublet approximation also substantially reduces the computational cost, by a factor of ~55 for the GW analysis and by ~12 for cosmological likelihood evaluations, yielding an estimated reduction of ~55 in the total computational cost of the combined analysis. Our results show the potential of DALI-based approximations to provide accurate and computationally efficient tools for forecasting in bright siren cosmology.

papers.title: Toric gravitational instantons with four fixed points
papers.abstract: We classify the simply connected toric gravitational instantons whose torus action has four fixed points. They are the hyperk\"ahler multi-Eguchi--Hanson and multi-Taub--NUT metrics with four collinear centres, the asymptotically flat instantons on Li and Sun's manifold $X_3$, up to scale one for each twist at infinity in $(0,1)$ for a fixed orientation of the torus, and, up to scale, a single further instanton with an ALF end, which is not hyperk\"ahler. The last two are Hermitian for neither orientation. In particular, the toric asymptotically flat instanton on $X_3$ with a given twist is unique up to scale, as conjectured by Li and Sun. The proof combines the solitonic form of Geroch's conjecture, which turns smoothness into polynomial equations for the soliton data, with a convexity principle adapted from Aksteiner. At a fixed asymptotic parameter, the cone errors of the conical metrics with a given rod structure are the gradient of a strictly convex function of the rod lengths, and the strict convexity gives uniqueness. Existence follows from an explicit solution for the ALF end and, for the AF ends, from Li and Sun's existence theorem. We also outline how a chart of Aksteiner identifies these AF instantons with those found by Teo.

papers.title: SN 2019qem: decades of extreme mass loss before the explosion of a luminous, long-lived Type IIn supernova
papers.abstract: We present the luminous, long-lived Type IIn SN 2019qem and use it to reconstruct how much mass its progenitor lost and when. We combine host-subtracted optical and mid-infrared photometry and 26 optical spectra from -22 to +699 d. We model the bolometric light curve with thin-shell CSM-interaction models in REDBACK, with the shock velocity constrained by the H$\alpha$ line widths, and compare them with an analytic interaction model. SN 2019qem rose in $\approx30$d to $M_I = -20.5$mag and a bolometric peak of $7.0\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and radiated $6.9\times10^{50}$ erg in the optical within 575 d, closely resembling luminous, strongly interacting SNe IIn such as SN 2010jl and SN 2015da. A Heii/Niii flash feature at -22 d and unresolved narrow Balmer lines reveal dense, slow CSM. From +78 to +445 d the H$\alpha$ wings are shaped by electron scattering, and the line stays blueshifted by 400-700 km s$^{-1}$, which points to an optically thick, asymmetric interaction region rather than to newly formed dust. In the preferred model, $\approx7 M_\odot$ of ejecta run into $\approx9 M_\odot$ of gas ejected $\approx2$ yr before explosion and then into a wind of $\approx0.6 M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ (for $v_w = 100$ km s$^{-1}$), sweeping up $\approx32 M_\odot$ by +544 d. The mid-infrared excess brightens for two years while the optical fades, tracing dust heated by the ongoing interaction. The host is a low-mass, star-forming galaxy, $\log(M_*/M_\odot) = 9.19$, with a sub-solar metallicity at the explosion site. In its final decades the progenitor of SN 2019qem lost mass far faster than any steady stellar wind, ending with an eruption of $\approx9 M_\odot$ two years before core collapse, consistent with luminous-blue-variable-like eruptive mass loss. Taken at face value, the mass budget implies an initial progenitor mass of $\gtrsim40 M_\odot$.

papers.title: Electromagnetic signatures of gradual magnetic dissipation in jets from supermassive black holes
papers.abstract: Context. Blazar jets -- collimated and relativistic plasma outflows viewed at small angles -- are prolific sources of non-thermal radiation. Aims. We develop a numerical framework for calculating the emission from an extended blazar jet where gradual energy dissipation, mediated through magnetic reconnection, takes place across a wide range of distances from the supermassive black hole. Methods. We adapt the open-source radiative transfer code LeHaMoC that self-consistently calculates photon spectra from relativistic charged particles that occupy a spherical blob to treat the emission from an extended jet. The jet is treated as a series of segments that interact with each other through radiative transfer. The effects of radiation spillage are calculated iteratively throughout the jet, accounting for relativistic effects arising from the relative motion between jet segments, until a steady state is reached. Results. We find that this approach produces some distinct differences in the total spectral energy distribution compared to the results obtained by adding the emission escaping from each constituent segment of the jet (optical thin regime), increasing the part of the spectrum affected by inverse Compton scattering by a factor of three. However, the latter is always far less luminous than the synchrotron component, even when enhanced by external radiation fields. Conclusions. Gradual magnetic dissipation in jets from supermassive black holes leads to nearly universal, synchrotron-dominated photon spectra. The numerical framework developed here is readily adaptable to a broad range of jet dissipation scenarios and applications to extended jet emission.

papers.title: Black Hole Mass Estimation of a Background Quasar in the Vicinity of the cD Galaxy Holm 15A
papers.abstract: This study analyzes spectra from the central region of the galaxy cluster Abell 85 observed with GTC/OSIRIS, focusing on the cD galaxy Holm 15A and the point-like X-ray source SDSS J004150.75-091824.3, projected $13.74\arcsec$ from Holm 15A. For the latter, we found it is a background quasar with a redshift of $1.56386 \pm 0.00397$, ruling out the possibility of it being a rogue BH gravitationally bound to Holm 15A. In addition, using single-epoch spectroscopy, we report that the quasar J004150 hosts a Supermassive Black Hole (SMBH) with a mass of $\log(M_{\text{BH}}/\mathrm{M_{\odot}}) = 8.72 \pm 0.26$.

papers.title: Radiative relativistic reconnection powering the hard-state emission of X-ray binaries: synchrotron-driven pair loading, MeV tail, and seed photons
papers.abstract: In the hard state, X-ray emission from black hole X-ray binaries is attributed to Comptonization in the corona, a highly magnetized region near the black hole. Relativistic magnetic reconnection drives bulk motions that can upscatter soft photons and reproduce the spectral peak at $\sim 100$ keV for parameters relevant to Cygnus X-1. However, the origin of the seed photons and of the MeV tail above the peak remains unclear. In 3D reconnection, so-called "free" particles escape the flux ropes and accelerate at the maximum rate set by the reconnection electric field. Their synchrotron emission extends to tens of MeV, which enables $\gamma \gamma$ pair production with the Compton-upscattered photons. We present 3D particle-in-cell simulations of relativistic reconnection in pair plasma, in which particles cool by inverse Compton (IC) scattering below the synchrotron self-absorption threshold and by synchrotron radiation above it. Of the incoming magnetic power, $\sim 40 \%$ is converted to IC radiation and $\gtrsim 10$-$20\%$ to synchrotron. Using analytical estimates and radiative calculations for Cygnus X-1, we model how the radiation from reconnection-accelerated particles is reprocessed in the corona. Pair production attenuates the synchrotron emission above $\sim 1$ MeV, and the escaping $\gamma$-rays form an MeV tail consistent with the observations, extending up to at least $\sim 10$ MeV. Most of the absorbed power goes into secondary pairs, whose Thomson optical depth can reach order unity. Their synchrotron emission, peaking at $\sim 0.1 \, \text{keV}$, can supply the seed photons for Comptonization. Our results support reconnection-based synchrotron self-Compton models of the hard-state emission in X-ray binaries.

papers.title: Metamorphic novae. I. Gaia22alz -- Violent relaxation starting from static evolution
papers.abstract: Gaia22alz (nova Vel 2022) shows characteristic properties in its light curves and spectral evolution similar to slow novae HR Del, V723 Cas, and V5558 Sgr. Their outburst begins in a way of hydrostatic expansion with no mass loss, followed by large amplitude ($\Delta V \sim 2$ mag) multiple peaks around the mean magnitude of $M_V \sim -5.5$, and eventually it decays similarly to normal classical novae. We present a light curve model of Gaia22alz based on our metamorphic nova theory: a nova starts from a static expansion and then metamorphoses to an optically thick wind evolution through a large amplitude multiple peak phase as a violent relaxation process. Our theoretical light curve for the rising phase consistently explains the slow rise and early spectral evolution of Gaia22alz. Gaia22als is a close binary as well as other three novae, which is consistent with our metamorphic nova theory that the companion motion in the nova envelope triggers the metamorphic transition. Our results do not support E. Aydi et al.'s explanation that the slow optical rise of Gaia22alz is owing to the irradiation of X-ray/UV flash.

papers.title: A detailed star formation history of the distant Milky Way satellite Canes Venatici I: An old dwarf spheroidal forming most of its stars after reionisation
papers.abstract: Canes Venatici I (CVnI) is a distant Milky Way (MW) dwarf spheroidal (dSph) satellite. To date, there is no consensus on its evolution and the properties of its stellar population. This work is aimed at obtaining an accurate picture of the star formation history (SFH) and metallicity distribution of CVnI to reconstruct its evolution in detail, as well as to infer the possible effects of internal and external feedback. We used archival HST/ACS observations to obtain the deepest colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) to date, reaching $\sim$2 mag below the old main sequence turn-off. We derived the SFH and metallicity distribution of CVnI using a state-of-the-art CMD-fitting technique. We found that the SFH is dominated by a single star formation period, which peaked around 11.8 Gyr ago, well after the reionisation epoch, and remained active until $\sim$10.4 Gyr ago. The galaxy's global metallicity, [Z/H], ranges from -2.4 to -1.5 dex. Interestingly, while its star population is old and metal-poor, compared to other MW satellites of a similar size and luminosity that formed most of their stars in a single burst, CVnI experienced a delayed star formation period. We carried out an exhaustive set of tests with synthetic and real populations to ensure the reliability of these results. We suggest that the evolution of CVnI could have been regulated by its mass accretion history. The galaxy would have evolved above (but still close to) a theoretic redshift-dependent critical mass above which it is possible to maintain star formation. The combined effect of SN feedback would have made CVnI's halo mass subcritical at z$\approx$2, definitively quenching its star formation. We cannot rule out the possible influence of gravitational interaction of CVnI with the MW at early ages, as hinted at by the most recent calculations of its orbit.

papers.title: Kerr metric perturbations in Lorenz gauge via numerical relativity methods
papers.abstract: Gravitational self-force calculations are needed to accurately describe the motion of a small body in a spinning (Kerr) black hole spacetime, which is vital to predict gravitational wave signals from asymmetric-mass compact binaries. Accurate calculations for the upcoming LISA mission require a minimum of second perturbative order in the mass ratio, which has thus far only been achieved for nonspinning (Schwarzschild) black holes due to nonlinear complexities of the Einstein equations. In this work, we calculate Kerr metric perturbations with a new computational approach based on numerical relativity methods, extending recent scalar self-force results to full general relativity. We formulate the perturbative Lorenz-gauge Einstein equations in terms of azimuthal $m$-modes in the frequency domain and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using a spectral discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and preconditioned iterative solvers. With our new method, we achieve exponentially convergent first-order gravitational self-force calculations for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime up to spin $|a|/M=0.998$ (the Thorne limit). Our framework is designed to carry over to second order by delivering accurate and well-behaved first-order data for nonlinear source construction, and as a solver for the second-order metric perturbations themselves.

papers.title: CCAT: Prime-Cam Control System and Related Software
papers.abstract: Prime-Cam is one of the primary instruments being developed for use by the CCAT collaboration with the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST), which is undergoing construction at a height of 5600 m in Cerro Chajnantor. Prime-Cam can host up to seven instrument modules with kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs), including broadband modules ranging 280-850 GHz and imaging spectrometers for line-intensity mapping. Prime-Cam requires a number of hardware devices for standard operation and data collection, and so a distributed control system must be developed for software integration of these devices and user-friendliness when controlling Prime-Cam in the field, especially during remote operation that will be typical during observations. The Prime-Cam Control System (PCS) is being developed using the Observatory Control System (OCS) framework originally developed for Simons Observatory (SO) and is adapted for Prime-Cam and CCAT-specific requirements. Within OCS/PCS, hardware devices are controlled individually by long-running software processes known as agents, which are typically deployed in Docker containers running in the background of one of the Prime-Cam network computers. These agents are controlled by client scripts through the command line or frontend tools like Nextline and PCS-web. PCS also makes use of several external open source software tools for remote operations, data management, and logging. This system is being tested in the lab in preparation for deployment in 2026 for use with Prime-Cam on FYST.

papers.title: A semi-autonomous multi-agent pipeline for high-energy astrophysics research with enforced provenance and verifiable self-extension
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are now applied to astronomical data analysis. They retrieve the literature, reduce observations, and draft conclusions. Under pressure to complete a task, such agents can fabricate results, and the numbers they report may not come from the analysis they ran. We present auto_research, a semi-autonomous multi-agent pipeline that retrieves and analyses raw data from the High Energy Astrophysics Science Archive Research Center (HEASARC) and writes the analysis tools that it needs. We check the work of the agents at two points. A new tool enters the toolkit after it passes automatic checks, including repeated test runs and a scan for phrases that accompany invented values, and a code review by a model from a different provider; a human decides whether to promote it to the trusted branch. A number in a report passes only if a recorded output of a toolkit tool or the request contains it, or if the report gives its location in a cited paper. We test the pipeline with data from the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE). Of 65 defects that we planted in the toolkit, 47 pass the automatic checks, and one passes the code review as well; the review also rejects 40 of 69 correct changes. The pipeline reproduces the published IXPE results for Cyg X-1: all 14 compared quantities agree within 3 sigma, and the polarization degrees are lower than the published values. With weaker models in the main roles, the pipeline recovers 12 of the 14 quantities and reports the other two as not measured. We also used the pipeline for a polarization-stability analysis of six observations, a survey of polarization against hardness in 29 observations, and a search for a time lag between the Stokes parameters q and u.

papers.title: Dirac stars in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg theory
papers.abstract: We study self-gravitating configurations of a charged classical spinor field coupled to gravity and to Euler-Heisenberg (EH) nonlinear electrodynamics, truncated at quartic order. The spinor is gauged under a U(1) field and may carry a quartic self-interaction. For static and spherically symmetric configurations we derive the field equations, reduce them to a dimensionless eigenvalue problem for the spinor frequency and solve it numerically. In the uncharged limit our solutions coincide with the known Dirac stars of general relativity. The electric charge increases the frequency, the mass and the size of the stars, and the maximal mass grows from $0.709$ to $1.027$ (in units of $M_{\rm Pl}^2/\mu$) when the charge coupling rises from zero to $0.75$. The quartic term changes the relation between the electric field and the enclosed charge, so that the field inside the star is weaker than in the Maxwell case. Our central result concerns stars with the same number of fermions, and therefore the same total charge. For them the quartic term changes the mass by less than $0.2\%$, but it makes the stars more compact and more strongly bound and shifts the turning point of the family to a smaller particle number. This shift is what lowers the maximal mass, by $9\%$ (from $0.924$ to $0.840$) at charge coupling $0.6$ as the dimensionless EH coupling goes from zero to $200$. In the weak-field regime of quantum electrodynamics (QED) the relative mass correction is $-1.5\times10^{-5}(E_{\max}/E_c)^2$, so the larger couplings describe the quartic model as an effective nonlinear electrodynamics rather than a controlled QED correction. All solutions satisfy the null, weak, strong and dominant energy conditions, show a positive pressure anisotropy, and remain free of horizons. Their stability is discussed through the binding energy and the turning point of the mass curve.

papers.title: Full-Stokes response to a stochastic gravitational-wave background in pulsar timing arrays: Fully analytic overlap reduction functions at finite distance and coherence of close pulsar pairs
papers.abstract: We derive fully analytic overlap reduction functions for the full-Stokes response of a pulsar timing array to an anisotropic tensor gravitational-wave background in general relativity. The response retains both pulsar distances and their complete propagation phases. At each fixed finite sky multipole, the intensity and circular polarization responses reduce to finite combinations involving exponential integrals and logarithms, while the electric and magnetic linear polarization responses require only elementary functions. We evaluate all components through $\ell=8$. Symmetry separates exact nulls from additional Earth-term nulls that propagation can lift. Even an unpolarized background can produce an imaginary cross-spectrum. For a pair with three-dimensional separation $d$, the pulsar terms can remain coherent when $2\pi fd/c\lesssim1$, even if both pulsars are many wavelengths from Earth. A uniform approximation retaining all four Earth and pulsar terms connects this regime to the short-wavelength limit, and a rotationally invariant relation fixes the leading transverse magnetic response. Common-distance errors cancel from the aligned pair phase, while relative-depth errors directly affect coherence. Under Gaussian differential averaging, fixed low-multipole norms and the squared norm summed over all multipoles decay at different rates as the response shifts to higher multipoles. Published pulsar configurations illustrate the roles of distance accuracy, bandwidth, and timing fits. At fixed pointwise intensity, a polarization covariance bound and a relative-depth noise budget quantify when differencing suppresses the background. Independent sky integration and matched-accuracy benchmarks test the analytic expressions over the parameter ranges studied.

papers.title: Signature of exocomet transits observed with Ariel
papers.abstract: We investigate the potential of the Ariel space telescope to detect and characterise exocomet transits through their wavelength-dependent photometric signatures. Building on a radiative-transfer framework, we model exocomet transits for three representative dust morphologies, three grain-size distributions, and four homogeneous dust compositions using synthetic photometric bands covering the Ariel wavelength range. The modelled events typically last 1-2 days and produce photometric variations of a few millimagnitudes. We find that the wavelength dependence of the transit signal provides stronger diagnostics of the dust properties than transit morphology alone. In particular, colour variations relative to the VISPhot band and their wavelength-dependent slopes separate the considered compositions into two broad groups: carbonaceous dust and graphite, and olivine and pyroxene. While the compositions within each group show similar behaviour, the two groups remain distinguishable across the dust morphologies and grain sizes considered. We further assess the detectability of these signals using the $\beta$~Pictoris spectral energy distribution and ArielRad simulations. Integrating over broad synthetic photometric bands substantially improves the signal-to-noise ratio, allowing millimagnitude-level signals to be detected with short integration times for sufficiently bright targets. Ariel's simultaneous optical-to-infrared coverage therefore offers the possibility not only of detecting exocomet transits, but also of characterising their chromatic signatures and constraining broad classes of dust properties. We also discuss the limitations of the modelling assumptions and the potential of coordinated observations with long-baseline photometric missions.

papers.title: Excitation factors and exceptional points of Kerr--Newman quasinormal modes
papers.abstract: We study excitation factors and investigate exceptional points (EPs) of Kerr--Newman quasinormal modes using the exact separated gravitoelectromagnetic equations. At fixed charge, the magnitudes of the excitation factors for the gravitational-led modes studied here decrease with increasing spin, whereas those for electromagnetic-led modes exhibit both monotonic and nonmonotonic behavior. The magnitude of the excitation factor for the first overtone can be comparable to or larger than that for the fundamental mode. We identify 42 EPs at which pairs of modes coalesce in the gravitational-led and electromagnetic-led sectors. Some EPs form sequences involving successive overtone pairs, with higher-overtone pairs coalescing progressively closer to the extremal limit. The additional EPs identified outside these sequences all share the same mode-pair labels as sequence members, but occur at different values of the black hole spin and charge. These findings clarify how rotation and charge shape the relative excitation strengths of different modes and the pattern of mode coalescence in the non-Hermitian spectrum of Kerr--Newman black holes.

papers.title: The Galah survey and symbiotic stars. II. Discovery, validation, and intensive follow-up of 44 new systems accreting at the lowest detectable levels
papers.abstract: We report the discovery, validation, and characterization of 44 new symbiotic stars (SySts) accreting at the lowest detectable levels (Lacc =< 3 Lsun). Candidates were initially selected from the Galah survey among non-pulsating M-type red giants exhibiting Halpha excess. Between 2021 and 2025, these targets were subjected to intensive multi-wavelength campaigns, including ground-based, high-resolution Echelle spectroscopy over 544 nights, multi-epoch flickering searches down to 1 mmag, and UV/X-ray observations with the Swift satellite. Our high-resolution spectra allowed for a detailed investigation of Halpha flux and line-profile variability. Crucially, the radial velocities measured for the M-giant components yielded reliable spectroscopic orbits for 22 objects and preliminary orbits for an additional eight, corroborated by binary-induced modulations in ASAS-SN photometry. Measured accretion levels vary by factors of up to 20X, emphasizing the need for high-sensitivity, long-term monitoring. Swift X-ray data exclude neutron star companions in all targets, consistent with predominance of white-dwarf degenerates in known SySts. Combined with the 33 objects from Paper I, this sample of 77 new SySts significantly exceeds the number of previously known, accreting-only Galactic symbiotic stars, constituting the bulk of the low-accretion (LowAcc) variety discovered to date and representing >10 percent of all known SySts in the Galaxy. As SySts likely spend most of their lifetimes in LowAcc faint states, characterizing this population is essential for estimating the total Galactic SySt population and evaluating the role of SySts as Type Ia supernova progenitors or sources of UV excess in elliptical galaxies.

papers.title: Response to "Late Time Dynamical Dark Energy and the CMB-Distance Ladder Tension"
papers.abstract: We respond to the recent paper by Efstathiou (arXiv:2607.29562) who makes several statements that appear to be in conflict with our recent paper (Turner & Huterer, arXiv:2606.05358). We stand by our primary result that direct determinations of $H_0$ can be sensitive to the late-time expansion history. We also point out where there is significant agreement between his work and ours.

papers.title: Cosmological evolution and late-time attractors in axion-monopole interacting dark energy
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological dynamics of axion-monopole interacting dark energy, examining whether a microscopically motivated dark-sector interaction can sustain stable late-time acceleration. In particular, magnetic monopoles constitute dark matter and an ultralight axion contributes to dark energy, with their interaction arising from the Witten effect through field-dependent dyon masses. We formulate the autonomous system, classify its critical points and stability, and investigate the evolution analytically and numerically. We find that stable de Sitter attractors at finite positive Hubble parameter require a positive cosmological constant and correspond to axion-potential minima, whereas those at maxima are unstable. Nevertheless, transient axion-driven acceleration remains possible without an explicit cosmological constant. Furthermore, the interaction induces matter-era tracking, namely an attracting slow-drift regime rather than an exact critical point. The interaction-effective dark-energy equation of state can cross the phantom divide, although the physical equation of state remains non-phantom. Extending the analysis to the full Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield dyon mass, we find that the main dynamical features persist, while the field evolution and interaction strength depend on the microscopic dyon properties. Our results demonstrate how a microscopically motivated dark-sector interaction can give rise to distinctive cosmological evolution and effective dark-energy behavior.

papers.title: Constraining tau-sterile neutrino mixing with high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
papers.abstract:
Whether a sterile neutrino mixes with the three active ones remains an open question. Its mixing with the tau neutrino, $|U_{	au 4}|^2$, is the least constrained, since terrestrial experiments probe it only indirectly and over limited ranges of sterile-neutrino mass. We show that TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos probe it differently. Their sources make almost no $
u_	au$, but oscillations over cosmological distances turn about one third of them into $
u_	au$ before they reach Earth. Mixing with a sterile neutrino would make these $
u_	au$ scarcer, lowering the $
u_	au$ fraction that neutrino telescopes measure, whatever the sterile-neutrino mass. In contrast, sterile mixing with $
u_e$ or $
u_\mu$ is nearly undetectable. Fitting the flavor composition measured by IceCube, with the composition at the sources left free, we find $|U_{	au 4}|^2 < 0.88$ at 90% C.L. Combining IceCube with present and planned neutrino telescopes, including IceCube-Gen2 and HUNT, could lower this limit to 0.24-0.29 by 2040 and to 0.12-0.14 by 2050. By 2050, these limits would match some present terrestrial limits, though not the strongest.

papers.title: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Data-Efficient Neural Surrogates for Amortized Physics Simulation
papers.abstract: Many scientific simulations are computationally expensive, limiting their use in simulation-based inference, uncertainty quantification, and decision making. We introduce macrocanonical generator networks, a framework for learning fast, data-efficient neural surrogates for amortized simulation of stationary physical processes by matching multiscale statistics of a target process. Inspired by microcanonical maximum-entropy synthesis, which matches feature statistics per sample by inner-loop optimization, our approach instead trains a neural generator to satisfy the same constraints in expectation, preserving physically realistic sample-to-sample fluctuations. We prove that gradient-descent training induces preconditioned gradient-descent dynamics in sample space that inherit the symmetry-preservation properties of the microcanonical gradient descent of Bruna and Mallat, amortizing its per-sample inner-loop optimization into a single training run after which every sample is generated in one forward pass. We further show that residual generator parameterizations initialized near the identity, trained with a small learning rate, preserve entropy locally during early optimization and mitigate mode collapse. Experiments on cosmology and fluid simulations show that macrocanonical generators recover realistic samples from extremely small training sets, in some cases a single training example, while generating new realizations more than $10^6$ times faster per sample than the reference simulator and more than $10^3$ times faster than microcanonical gradient descent. The trained generators can be reused for downstream pretraining, including simulation-based inference, providing a data-efficient route to multi-fidelity scientific machine learning workflows.

papers.title: Gravitational-wave lensing beyond the diffraction integral: proper-time methods and the bound lens
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) can have wavelengths comparable to the Schwarzschild radius of their lenses, and detectors record their phase, so lensing requires wave optics. Its standard tool, the diffraction integral, follows from the particle path integral of a scalar wave on a static weak field, under the eikonal (one-way) and paraxial approximations, plus the thin-lens limit. We give a self-contained account of how the proper-time (worldline) representation overcomes these steps. An auxiliary proper time makes the wave equation exactly first order, with frequency as $1/\hbar$, so geometric optics and, for paraxial thin-lens paths, the diffraction integral follow from stationarity of an exact integral. For a point mass, the Duru-Kleinert (DK) gauge and Kustaanheimo-Stiefel map give the exact propagator; for a distant observer the DK time and fibre angle become the radius and azimuth of a lens plane, the result is the point-lens amplification factor with the offset set by the excess path, and geometric optics requires $w\gg1$ and $wy\gg1$. This agreement reflects the Coulomb potential, not the approximations: the exact eikonal condition, $\varepsilon_E\simeq\bar\lambda/d+GM/c^2d+\mathcal O(\sin^2\theta/2)$, fails near the lens and at large angles, and the one-way step is a non-relativistic limit. We then treat the bound lens, a GW source orbiting its lens, which emits a backscattered echo and moves during the lensing delays. Its exact time-domain signal gives each worldline its own retarded time and Doppler factor, so no single amplification factor describes it. In the diffraction regime the Shapiro phase alone misses all lensing beyond it, geometric optics misses 46-100% of it near conjunction at $w=0.3$, the paraxial geometry fails on the far side, and the static amplification factor along the orbit errs by $\approx(1-2)\,wM/R$ near conjunction and by the echo amplitude elsewhere.

papers.title: First application of the optimised next neighbour cleaning to data from imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes
papers.abstract: Imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs) cameras are constantly subject to signals from the night sky background and electronic noise during event recordings. Image cleaning methods are typically employed to eliminate pixels that are mostly noise-contaminated and lack sufficient Cherenkov light. In this paper, we present the implementation of the optimised next neighbour (ONN) technique to the Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System (VERITAS) reconstruction pipeline. With this method, cleaning thresholds are derived in a two-parameter space, composed of the minimum total integrated charge of a cluster of pixels, $q_{\rm min}$, and by the maximum difference in the pulse arrival time within the cluster, $\delta_t$. The cleaning contours in $q_{\rm min} - \delta_t$ are adjusted to set a high probability of noise suppression while optimising the retention of pixels containing Cherenkov light. In comparison to the VERITAS double-pass image cleaning method, effective areas are increased at the lower energy range ($\sim$ 60 - 90 GeV) by a factor of up to $\sim$ 25. Energy thresholds are reduced by up to $\sim$ 22\%. Testing the method on Crab Nebula data resulted in an increased number of reconstructed excess events at energies < 1 TeV by a factor of up to $\sim$ 82. Finally, an increase in the differential sensitivity of VERITAS by a factor of up to $\sim$ 8 was observed at $\sim$ 20 GeV. With the addition of BDT-based $\gamma$/hadron separation cuts, the method improves the detection significance of a 20 hour Crab Nebula dataset, while excess event rates are enhanced by $\sim$ 16\%. In summary, the ONN image cleaning provides a reduced energy threshold and a higher rate of event reconstruction. The technique is especially advantageous for the analysis of gamma-ray sources presenting transient and soft spectra.

papers.title: Linear perturbation theory and structure formation in a Horndeski theory of gravity without dark matter
papers.abstract: We study the formation and evolution of the cosmic large-scale structure (LSS) in a scalar-tensor Horndeski theory of gravity without dark matter. We impose that this theory reduces to Refracted Gravity (RG) in the weak-field limit. RG is a non-relativistic theory where the gravitational permittivity $\epsilon(\rho)$, with $\rho$ the baryonic matter density, provides the gravitational boost required to describe both the dynamics of galaxies and galaxy clusters without dark matter. We show that $\epsilon(\rho)$ equals the function $G_4(\varphi)$ of the scalar field $\varphi$ of our Horndeski model. The background evolution of a flat, matter-dominated, homogeneous and isotropic universe shows that $\varphi$ is also responsible for the accelerated expansion of the universe and that the model is capable of reproducing the observed redshift evolution of the Hubble-Lema\^itre parameter. We finally develop the linear perturbation theory and study the growth factor equation. The model fails to correctly describe the LSS by predicting a late onset of the formation of cosmic structure at redshift $z\lesssim 1$.

papers.title: Chiral anomalies in two dimensions
papers.abstract: Chiral anomalies offer a fundamental probe of the quantum structure of gauge theories and their underlying symmetries. In this paper, we introduce a framework to characterize the chiral anomaly in two dimensions directly at the diagrammatic level. To this end, we establish a consistent prescription for handling $\gamma^5$ in dimensional regularization at $d=2$. On this basis, we derive an expression for the fully generic chiral anomaly directly from the contributions of the bubble and triangle diagrams, either in the massless or massive case. Then, we show that the different forms of the anomaly can arise from appropriate choices of parameters directly at the level of this master expression. Overall, $d=2$ is shown to provide an excellent environment to investigate chiral anomalies at the amplitude level: Ward identities are demonstrated rigorously and to arbitrary order in the mass expansion without further approximation, resulting in an unprecedented degree of control on the anomaly.

papers.title: Scale-Dependent Weak-Field Dynamics in Horndeski Theory: Galaxy Rotation Curves and Turnaround Scales
papers.abstract: In this work, the weak-field dynamics of a gravitational-wave compatible subclass of Horndeski gravity is investigated on galactic and intergalactic scales. The analysis is performed within the weak-field approximation for stationary and approximately spherically symmetric configurations, retaining the nonlinear scalar derivative interactions responsible for scale-dependent modifications of the gravitational field. On galactic scales, the transition regime is investigated through the effective potential, the stability of circular orbits, galaxy rotation curves, and the relation between dynamical and lensing masses. The analysis shows that the scalar field modifies the orbital dynamics and the radial dependence of the rotational velocity, while generating a nonvanishing gravitational slip between the dynamical and lensing mass estimates. On intergalactic scales, the asymptotic weak-field dynamics is investigated and a turnaround scale is derived from the balance between the effective gravitational attraction and the large-scale curvature contribution. At large distances, the asymptotic gravitational field is governed by the background curvature contribution.

papers.title: von Neumann Stability Analysis of Braginskii MHD Thermal Conduction, Viscosity, Magnetic Diffusion, and Thermoelectric Effects and an Implementation in Athena++
papers.abstract: Athena++ is a finite-volume astrophysical magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code. As of writing, isotropic thermal conduction and kinematic viscosity, Ohmic resistivity, and ambipolar diffusion are present in the main branch. Here we present a fork of Athena++, ``Athena-Aniso''. It implements fully anisotropic thermal conduction (parallel, perpendicular, and the Righi--Leduc effect); anisotropic viscosity (all five Braginskii viscosity tensors); the Hall effect; and several thermoelectric effects (Peltier, Seebeck, Nernst, and Ettingshausen). These effects can be weighted by ionisation fraction in a partially ionised gas, with the neutral part diffusing isotropically. We have also added isotropic bulk viscosity. The Biermann battery is not implemented here. The dissipative terms have super-time-stepping support, while the non-dissipative terms are combined with the ideal MHD flux. A CFL condition for all terms is derived and implemented using von Neumann stability analysis. The dissipative terms are found to be stable under first-order time integration. The non-dissipative terms are found to be stable under third-order time integration. We additionally derive new signal speeds for a modified HLLE Riemann solver. These suppress grid-scale non-linear instabilities still present in the non-dissipative terms. The Nernst/Ettingshausen system is found to be ill-posed unless it is stabilised by both perpendicular thermal conduction and perpendicular magnetic diffusion. We derive a well-posedness criterion for this. We provide numerical tests of each implemented effect against derived analytical solutions.

papers.title: Does Topology-Dependent Chemistry Influence the Interstellar PAH Inventory? Insights from the Absence of Cyanotriphenylenes
papers.abstract: Although a set of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) has recently been identified in the cold dark cloud TMC-1, several common PAH motifs remain absent, leaving the origin of this apparent structural selectivity unresolved. Triphenylene (\ce{C18H12}) provides a stringent test of whether relative thermodynamic stability alone can account for the emerging PAH inventory because it is the smallest fully benzenoid PAH predicted by Clar's rule, is exceptionally stable, and is a key subunit of larger detected aromatic frameworks such as coronene and fullerene-related species. To probe whether such thermodynamically favored carbon skeletons are selected under cold interstellar conditions, we synthesized cyanotriphenylenes and measured their first 6.5--16~GHz microwave rotational spectra as polar tracers for the non-polar parent. An astronomical search based on these spectroscopic parameters yielded no detection, suggesting a possible ``missing triphenylene'' anomaly: despite its exceptional thermodynamic stability, this fully benzenoid PAH may be relatively depleted in TMC-1. To rationalize this behavior, we introduce a ring-node graphic representation that classifies PAH skeletons by topology; within this framework, triphenylene, whose compactness is otherwise ambiguous, is classified as non-compact. This representation reveals a tentative clustering of the currently detected and undetected PAHs according to topology, suggesting that the current PAH inventory cannot be rationalized solely on the basis of thermodynamic stability and may instead reflect differences in formation and destruction kinetics. The observed selectivity may arise from two complementary effects: sequential growth decay along bottom-up growth pathways and rapid consumption of bay-region intermediates by reactive unsaturated small species.

papers.title: Horizon exchange and the universal all-spin response of Kerr
papers.abstract: The radial Teukolsky equation is invariant under exchange of the outer and inner horizons, although the physical boundary condition is not. We derive an exact monodromy relation between the corresponding Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi (MST) near-zone responses. At leading order in frequency and to all orders in spin, this relation yields, for every multipole, an expression for the leading horizon-exchange-odd response. For gravitational perturbations, it determines the exchange-odd contribution to quadrupolar absorption and organizes the exchange-even dynamical response into a digamma function whose expansion accounts for the odd- and even-zeta structures found in Kerr-Compton calculations. The exact relation, rather than the individual previously known small-spin coefficients, is the central result.

papers.title: Renormalization and Factorization Scale-Invariant Predictions for the $e^+e^- J/+_c$ process at $B$ factories
papers.abstract: We perform a NNLO perturbative QCD analysis for exclusive double charmonium production $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ within the NRQCD factorization formalism using the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC). It is well known that this charmonium process suffers poor pQCD convergence, as well as large renormalization scale uncertainty. The PMC is used to remove conventional renormalization scale uncertainty. Based on two fundamental physical processes of charmonium, $J/\psi\rightarrow e^+e^-$ and $\eta_c\rightarrow\gamma\gamma$, and using the NNLO perturbative results together with experimental measurements, we extract the factorization-scale-dependent long-distance matrix elements for $J/\psi$ and $\eta_c$. Combining these two matrix elements with the factorization-scale-dependent short-distance coefficient, we obtain predictions that are independent of the factorization scale for the $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ process. Our predictions agree with the measurement from the BaBar collaborations within errors. Remarkably, we provide a new way to eliminate conventional renormalization and factorization scale ambiguities for the $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ process. We further demonstrate that the slow convergence of the pQCD series is an intrinsic property of this double-charmonium process.

papers.title: Weyl Rescalings: A First Order Approach
papers.abstract: Weyl transformations, --local rescalings in which the metric transforms as $g_{\mu\nu}(x)\longrightarrow \Omega^2(x)\, g_{\mu \nu}(x)$--, are expected to be a symmetry of nature at extremely high energy, that should be (spontaneously) broken at low energy. In Cartan's first order formulation of gravity this translates into the condition that the local frames (vielbein) scale as $e^a(x) \longrightarrow \Omega(x) e^a(x)$. In this construction, the Lorentz connection one-form fields $\omega^a{}_b$ are independent from $e^a$, and since Lorentz transformations and dilatations commute, $\omega$ and $R(\omega)$ must be Weyl invariant, while in the second order metric formalism the Ricci tensor undergoes a non-homogeneous transformation. This generates a tension between the two formulations, which should be equivalent in the vanishing torsion limit. Here we show how the puzzle can be resolved taking into account the role of torsion. This also sheds some light on the conformal coupling of matter fields to gravity.

papers.title: The ALMA survey to Resolve exoKuiper belt Substructures (ARKS) XII. Constraints on large bodies embedded in discs
papers.abstract: The ALMA survey to Resolve exoKuiper belt Substructures (ARKS) presents detailed constraints on structure and properties of a sample of 24 debris discs at millimetre wavelengths, including measurements of vertical thicknesses for a subsample of discs. We estimated sizes and total masses of large bodies that feed collisional cascades producing the observed millimetre dust in 11 ARKS discs with a well constrained vertical thickness. Separately, we estimated the sizes and total masses of large bodies that could be gravitationally stirring these discs, assuming that such stirring is the origin of the vertical thickness. We used a semi-analytic particle-in-a-box collisional model and a semi-analytic model of stirring through gravitational scattering. We accounted for the dependence of collisional damping efficiency on the average collision velocity. We find that planetesimals feeding the collisional cascades are less than 20 km in size, while the total masses in the planetesimals are lower than 200 M$_\oplus$. There is a good agreement between minimum disc masses inferred from millimetre and infrared observations. The hypothetical stirrers are always larger in size than the planetesimals, but they do not necessarily contain most of the disc mass. In agreement with previous work, the observed dust masses can be explained by steady-state collisional models with reasonable disc masses. The measured vertical scale-heights can be explained by gravitational stirring from embedded large bodies of reasonable properties. However, more advanced models are needed to address the observed non-Gaussian vertical profiles, along with the dependence of disc scale-height on particle size and stellocentric distance.

papers.title: Probing the Spatial Coherence of Chiral-Imbalance Fluctuations with Hyperon Spin Correlations
papers.abstract: Topological fluctuations in the quark-gluon plasma can generate local chiral imbalances whose spatial coherence remains difficult to access with conventional charge-separation measurements. We propose differential hyperon-pair spin correlations as a probe of both the strength and spatial organization of these fluctuations. Fluctuations of the axial chemical potential $\mu_5$ can induce pair correlations even when the mean helicity polarization vanishes. Using the AMPT model, we find that the magnitude of the hyperon spin correlation probes the magnitude and spatial coherence scale of $\mu_5$, while the ratio of short- and long-range correlations varies strongly with the spatial coherence scale, but only weakly with $\mu_{5}$ over the range of explored parameters. These observables provide an experimentally testable strategy for constraining the spatial structure of chiral-imbalance fluctuations.

papers.title: Eigenfrequency sensitivity in nonadiabatic stellar pulsations
papers.abstract: We derive an adjoint formulation of eigenfrequency sensitivity for linear nonadiabatic stellar pulsations, including the frequency dependence of the boundary conditions. Local sensitivity kernels and their cumulative integrals describe the responses of the excitation rate and oscillation frequency to prescribed scaling of the pulsation matrix and its acoustic, thermal and coupling blocks. Applications to selected radial modes of post-AGB envelopes reveal distinct spatial and subsystem sensitivity profiles. In the cool model, the ordinary mode has weak sensitivity near both boundaries for the slow branch outer boundary conditions, whereas the strange mode exhibits pronounced sensitivity in the outer layers. Selected modes of the hotter model also show appreciable outer-layer sensitivity. The block decomposition reveals differing contributions and cancellations in the excitation-rate and oscillation-frequency responses.

papers.title: On Photon Propagation in Strong Magnetic Fields: Time Delays from Pulsars
papers.abstract: We study photon dispersion in the presence of a strong external magnetic field for propagation both perpendicular and parallel to the field, considering (i) the magnetized QED vacuum and (ii) a magnetized electron-positron medium at finite density (nonzero chemical potential). The analysis is performed in one-loop QED at finite temperature and density, and we extract polarization-dependent dispersion relations and phase velocities from the eigenmodes of the photon polarization operator. Using these phase velocities, we estimate propagation-induced time delays for photons emitted from neutron stars in the strong-field regime, adopting a simplified magnetosphere model with a toroidal magnetic field geometry and a radially varying chemical potential profile in the degenerate limit. We compare the predicted delays with observational timing constraints and discuss how strong-field QED and plasma corrections can generate measurable departures from the light cone, with potential signatures relevant for magnetars and modern polarimetric and timing observations. It should be noted that the time-delay estimates derived here are based on the phase velocity and serve as indicative order-of-magnitude predictions.

papers.title: Mixed-Order Parity-Violating Corrections to Rotating Black Holes in Combined Scalar Gauss-Bonnet and Dynamical Chern-Simons Gravity
papers.abstract: We construct the leading mixed-order $\mathcal{O}(\zeta_{\rm GB}\zeta_{\rm CS})$ deformation of rotating black holes in a combined scalar Gauss-Bonnet and dynamical Chern-Simons effective theory, the sector in which the parity-even and parity-odd corrections act simultaneously. Using a pseudospectral solution of the coupled mixed scalar and metric equations, we compute horizon and equatorial-geodesic observables--the horizon angular velocity, surface gravity, area, and Wald entropy; the innermost stable circular orbit and photon-ring radii; and photon-ring eikonal estimates of the ringdown--at fixed mass and angular momentum over the spin range $0.1\le a\le0.9$, where the solution is numerically convergent and the perturbative expansion is controlled for sufficiently small dimensionless couplings. We verify the exact Kerr and Schwarzschild limits, reproduce available pure-sector benchmarks, and quantify spectral, residual, and extraction uncertainties. The mixed solution satisfies every component of the field equations, including the one that is not imposed in its construction, and its Wald entropy satisfies the first law to about one part in $10^{5}$. The mixed coefficients exhibit spin dependence qualitatively distinct from the individual sectors within this EFT truncation. All four horizon quantities, and several orbital and eikonal ones, change sign as functions of spin. The ringdown results are leading photon-ring eikonal estimates; a full coupled finite-$\ell$ perturbation calculation is left to future work.

papers.title: Extended 2.25/8.60 GHz Observations of the Magnetar Swift J1818.0-1607
papers.abstract: We present the long-term rotational evolution and radio emission properties of the magnetar Swift~J1818.0$-$1607, using simultaneous 2.25/8.60~GHz observations obtained with the Shanghai Tian Ma Radio Telescope from MJD~58936 to 59427. The average pulse profiles exhibit significant evolution with time and frequency, attributable to relative changes in the leading, central, and trailing emission components. The magnetar generally spins down with an average rate of $-1.65(4)\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{s^{-2}}$, with the magnitude of the spin-down rate first increasing and then decreasing over the monitoring span. The overall flux density shows an initial rise followed by a decline, with sporadic variability superimposed; the variations at 2.25 and 8.60~GHz are broadly consistent across most epochs. The two-point spectral index increased from $\alpha\simeq-1.8$ shortly after the outburst to near-zero values around MJD~59030--59050, followed by repeated decreases and increases. Despite this variability, 41 of the 54 two-point spectral-index measurements in the later campaign have $\alpha>-1$. Three component-dependent types of mode changing are identified: Type~I, involving primarily intensity changes in the central component; Type~II, involving central and trailing components; and Type~III, involving leading and central components. All three classes include events showing a corresponding component response in the other observing band, with event-dependent response strengths and directions. Type~I variations are generally more pronounced at 8.60~GHz than at 2.25~GHz.

papers.title: Next-to-leading order QCD corrections to fully charm tetraquark radiative decays
papers.abstract: We present the first complete next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD calculation of the fully charm tetraquark radiative decays $T_{4c}(0^{++},2^{++})\to\gamma J/\psi$ and $T_{4c}(1^{+-})\to\gamma\eta_c$ at leading order in the relative velocity. The NLO widths are $2.3$--$3.1$ times the leading-order (LO) widths for the long-distance matrix element (LDME) inputs considered here, with $m_c=1.5$ GeV and $\mu_R=2m_c$. In the scalar channel, the NLO corrections change the relative contributions of the two color-spin components and their interference. For the tensor channel, the longitudinal fraction $f_L$ of the daughter $J/\psi$ changes from $0.11$ at LO to $0.18$ at strictly expanded NLO, with sensitivity to higher-order corrections. These NLO results provide valuable theoretical input for searches for states predicted below their respective lowest dicharmonium thresholds and for probing the spin and short-distance structure of observed tetraquark candidates.

papers.title: GAMA-23 deep field with uGMRT Band-2: source catalogue and source count
papers.abstract: We present the low-frequency GAMA-23 field of the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) survey with upgraded Giant Meterwave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) observations in Band-2 ($120-250$ MHz). The on-source observation was conducted for ${\sim}5$ hours. The final image achieved an off-source RMS noise of 320 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$, covering an area of $5.86\,\text{deg}^2$ with restoring beam size of $15.4''{\times}8.2''$ at the central frequency of 183 MHz. The catalogue derived from the radio image includes 569 sources with a flux density limit of ${\geq}\,5{\sigma}$. The flux density measurements and the positional accuracy are cross-verified and compared with other radio catalogues available in the literature. The spectral indices derived from fitting a power law are -0.68$^{+0.18}_{-0.23}$ for the ASKAP EMU catalogue and -0.72$^{+0.19}_{-0.24}$ for the NVSS catalogue. The normalised source count derived from this catalogue is consistent with models and observations with a nominal catalogue threshold of 1.7 mJy, while the sensitivity varies across the image.

papers.title: DAMA/LIBRA dark matter signal: a global analysis
papers.abstract: The annual modulation reported by the DAMA/LIBRA collaboration remains in tension with the null results of other direct-detection experiments. We investigate the compatibility of DAMA/LIBRA with LZ, PICO-60 and CDMSlite within a generalized non-relativistic effective field theory (EFT) framework. In addition to the EFT operator expansion we investigate additional modifications to the standard WIMP picture, including inelastic scattering, variations in the NaI quenching factors, and a rescaling of the dark-matter velocity dispersion. We perform a Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis in this extended model space, using two alternative approaches to the likelihood function describing the DAMA/LIBRA data. Both approaches result in strong discrepancy between the data from DAMA/LIBRA and other experiments. We conclude that the extended model space considered here cannot accommodate the DAMA/LIBRA signal while remaining consistent with the non-observation of dark matter in other experiments.

papers.title: Solar extreme-ultraviolet waves and other associated solar activities
papers.abstract: Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) waves are large-scale, tsunami like disturbances on the solar surface associated with eruptive phenomena such as solar flares, filament eruptions, and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Because their strong correlation with major solar eruptions, we present here a comprehensive statistical study of EUV waves and their connections to Moreton waves, CMEs, solar flares, type II radio bursts, and solar energetic particle (SEP) events during Solar Cycle 25 (December 2019-December 2025). This study utilizes EUV data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly onboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory and coronagraph data from the Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph onboard Solar and Heliospheric Observatory. Our analysis reveals that 12.3% of the observed EUV waves are associated with Moreton waves, 95% with CMEs, 92.7% associated with flares, 44.3% with metric type II radio bursts, and 11.8% with SEPs. While nearly all EUV waves are linked to CMEs, their association with solar flares varies significantly, ranging from weak B-class events to major X-class flares. Furthermore, the majority of Moreton waves correlate with large- or medium-class flares, with only a small fraction associated with weaker C-class flares. Our findings may contribute to a better understanding of space weather events and, potentially, to their forecasting.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Large-Scale Velocity Field from DESI DR1 with Bayesian Inference
papers.abstract: Survey boundaries and nonlinear dynamics complicate reconstruction of large-scale matter-density and peculiar-velocity fields from galaxy redshift surveys. We develop and compare two reconstruction methods within a common Bayesian framework, based on linear perturbation theory and the Zel'dovich approximation, and apply them to the DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey. We infer the initial density field using a Gaussian prior and likelihood, with the Zel'dovich model displacing particles from a uniform Lagrangian grid. Both yield maximum a posteriori (MAP) fields; only the linear posterior is sampled. Our main findings are: \textit{(i)} Both reconstructions yield similar large-scale density structures and coherent velocity patterns in the survey interior, beyond roughly \(50\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\) from the footprint boundaries. \textit{(ii)} Comparison with Cosmicflows-4 groups, predominantly from the SDSS Fundamental Plane sample in the DESI overlap, shows close agreement between mean observed radial velocities and MAP predictions when binned by the latter, despite substantial individual scatter. \textit{(iii)} Both yield similar reflex-dipole profiles, defined as mean shell velocities relative to those at randomly sampled centres, out to \(\sim225\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\). The profiles depend weakly on the prior normalization \(\sigma_8\), but lie below the fiducial linear \(\Lambda\)CDM reference at \(r<50\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}\). Sparse sampling limits the largest radii. \textit{(iv)} In an exploratory BAO test, shifting galaxies and randoms to a target redshift \(z=8\) using reconstructed displacements sharpens the acoustic feature in both cases, with a slightly more pronounced peak for Zel'dovich. Survey geometry and galaxy bias remain the principal limitations.

papers.title: On the Motion of a Point Electric Charge in the Field of Wu-Yang Monopoles in Bertotti-Robinson Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We study the $SU(2)$ Einstein-Yang-Mills system with non-minimal $RF^2$-type couplings of Yang-Mills fields to curvature, formulated with exterior differential forms and a Lagrange-multiplier constraint for the Levi-Civita connection. We show that the conformally flat Bertotti-Robinson geometry $AdS_2\times S^2$ carries the Wu-Yang magnetic pole as an exact solution for arbitrary non-minimal couplings; the couplings only renormalise the radius of the $S^2$. The non-conformally-flat branch of solutions known for this system is recalled. The Hopf fibration $S^3/S^2\cong S^1$ of the gauge group manifold projects the Wu-Yang field on a uniform Dirac-type magnetic field, and the motion of a point electric charge in it is solved in closed form: the charge moves on a cone and oscillates between the horizon and a maximal radius.

papers.title: Disruption limits around triaxial bodies and implications for ring-bearing minor bodies
papers.abstract: The classical Roche limit is often used as a boundary between ring-dominated and satellite-dominated regions, although it is derived for a self-gravitating fluid satellite orbiting a spherical primary. This assumption is poorly suited to ring-bearing minor bodies, which are often triaxial. Here, we compute the equilibrium figures and disruption limits of inviscid fluid satellites orbiting triaxial primaries, modelling their gravity fields through J2 and C22. The primary's oblateness and equatorial asymmetry shifts the disruption limit outward relative to the classical Roche limit, with C22 dominating the correction at sufficiently high values, which require highly oblate primaries. The disruption location also depends on the primary's orientation, defining a radial disruption region rather than a single limit in non-double-synchronous systems. Increasing orbital inclination shifts the limit inward, significantly so only at high inclinations. Symbolic regression provides an empirical expression for the disruption limit around triaxial primaries, which we apply to ring-bearing minor bodies. The correction is most relevant for Haumea and Chariklo, whereas the rings of Chiron and Quaoar located beyond the classical Roche limit remain outside the disruption region for realistic particle densities. This indicates that treating the disruption limit as a strict boundary between ring-dominated and satellite-dominated regions is an oversimplification, since the long-term survival of a ring also depends on collisional evolution, particle properties, and resonant confinement driven by the primary's non-axisymmetric gravity field.

papers.title: Investigating nucleon resonances in the $pp K^+K^+$ reaction
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the \(pp \to K^+ K^+ \Lambda \Lambda\) reaction using an effective Lagrangian approach and the isobar model. The calculation includes the exchange of \(\pi\), \(\eta\), \(\sigma\), \(\rho\), \(\omega\), and \(K\) mesons, as well as contributions from eight nucleon resonances: \(N(1535)\), \(N(1650)\), \(N(1710)\), \(N(1720)\), \(N(1895)\), \(N(1900)\), \(N(2060)\) and \(N(2120)\). The double-resonance excitation mechanism (\(NN \to N^* N^*\)) is found to dominate this reaction over the entire energy range considered. Among the exchanged mesons, the \(\eta\) exchange provides the largest contribution at lower energies, whereas the \(K\) exchange dominates at higher energies. Near the threshold, \(N(1535)\) and \(N(1650)\) play the most important roles, while at higher energies \(N(1710)\) and \(N(1720)\) become dominant. Due to isospin conservation, this reaction is predominantly coupled to nucleon resonances, providing a relatively clean channel for \(N^*\) spectroscopy. Our results indicate the unique potential of this reaction for studying nucleon resonances and provide a theoretical reference for future experimental studies at HIAF.

papers.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.

papers.title: The TNG50-SKIRT Atlas: Multi-wavelength properties of galaxy discs in the TNG50 simulation
papers.abstract: We investigate the wavelength dependence of disc scale lengths in galaxies from the TNG50-SKIRT Atlas (TSA), and assess whether the simulated galaxies reproduce the structural properties and scaling relations observed in real galaxies. We measure disc scale lengths from 1D radial surface-brightness profiles of multi-wavelength synthetic images. The disc-dominated region is defined interactively per galaxy and applied consistently across bands. We restrict the analysis to nearly face-on, star-forming galaxies and retain only systems whose r-band profiles are well described by an exponential model. The resulting scale lengths are compared to observational samples and analysed using both dust-attenuated and dust-free images, as well as intrinsic stellar population maps. We find that the majority of TSA galaxies exhibit exponential discs in realistic mock observations. TSA galaxies reproduce the observed disc scale length-stellar mass (luminosity) relation, but are systematically larger at fixed mass or luminosity. The dependence of disc scale length on morphology is weak. Disc scale lengths correlate strongly across wavelengths, but decrease systematically with increasing wavelength. When normalised by the stellar-mass scale length, TSA galaxies exhibit a monotonic trend consistent with observations over the optical-to-NIR range. Comparing dust-free and dust-attenuated images and linking the results to intrinsic galaxy properties, we find that stellar population gradients are the primary driver of this wavelength dependence. In particular, radial gradients in stellar age dominate the effect, while metallicity gradients play a secondary role. Dust attenuation further enhances the wavelength dependence at short wavelengths but is not its main origin. Residual offsets in absolute scale length indicate the remaining differences between simulated and observed galaxy structure.

papers.title: dSIBP: a package for generating IBP seeds for QFT in de Sitter spacetime
papers.abstract: Recent studies show that in addition to the flat spacetime, Integration-by-parts (IBP) relations and differential equations can also provide a systematic approach to Feynman integrals in de Sitter spacetime. dSIBP is a Mathematica package for the automated construction of IBP systems and differential equations. For dS integral families with massive and massless propagators, it generates a complete set of IBP seeds, assembles linear systems for external reduction, and constructs differential equations for the reduced master integrals. The implementation combines equations of motion, remaining terms and parity constraints, and provides reliable checks. We describe the conventions and public interface through worked examples.

papers.title: Limits to research in astrophysics
papers.abstract: Fundamental physics faces several intrinsic limitations, such as the finite speed of light in vacuum, the absolute zero temperature, Heisenberg's uncertainty principle and so on.
